questions.scenario: During a production run, the play recap shows `web-02 : ok=0 changed=0 unreachable=1 failed=0`, while another host completed tasks. What failed first for web-02? The rest of the fleet is waiting for the operator to classify this result before retrying.

options.text: The SSH or transport connection to web-02.
A module changed the wrong configuration file.
A handler failed after all tasks completed.
The playbook YAML parser rejected the file.

questions.explanation: An unreachable result means Ansible could not establish the connection needed to execute tasks on that host. It is different from a task failure after connection. See [Ansible error handling](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_error_handling.html).

questions.scenario: An orders configuration template reports `changed`, then the validation task fails with `unknown directive upstream`. Which evidence should the operator inspect first? The service must not restart until the team understands whether the candidate configuration is valid.

options.text: The fork count on the control node.
The rendered diff and the validator stderr.
The inventory group order.
The number of successful hosts only.

questions.explanation: The proposed template change and validation error are the most direct evidence about the failure. Increasing concurrency or ignoring the task would not repair the invalid candidate. See [Ansible error handling](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_error_handling.html).

questions.scenario: After an initial deployment changed several resources, the next successful run reports `ok=7 changed=0` on every host. What does that second result support? The team wants to distinguish useful convergence evidence from application-health evidence.

options.text: No managed host was contacted.
Every external dependency is healthy.
The play has converged for the managed state it checked.
The play can never fail in production.

questions.explanation: A quiet second run is useful evidence of idempotent convergence. It does not replace runtime health checks or prove future runs cannot fail. See [Ansible playbook introduction](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_intro.html).

questions.scenario: A Red Hat-only package task is reported as `skipped` on a Debian host, and its condition checks `ansible_facts.os_family == "RedHat"`. What is the expected interpretation? The same play also contains a Debian-specific task that runs successfully on this host.

options.text: The host was unreachable.
The task changed state but hid the result.
A handler already performed the task.
The condition evaluated false for that host.

questions.explanation: The condition excludes the task on hosts whose gathered operating-system family is not RedHat. Skipped is an execution decision, not a connection failure. See [Ansible error handling](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_error_handling.html).

questions.scenario: The play recap shows one failed task on web-01 and summarizes the counts for every host. Why should the operator also read the failed task result? The operator must choose the next investigation without rerunning the entire fleet blindly.

options.text: The recap is printed before tasks execute.
The task result contains the module message and failure context.
The recap never contains host names.
Only task output contains changed counts.

questions.explanation: The recap summarizes per-host counts. The failed task result carries the module return data needed to diagnose the problem. See [Ansible playbook output control](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/default_callback.html).
